$comment: DERIVED, not verbatim. Written by this library from the prose of the W3C Recommendation Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0 (REC-vc-data-model-2.0-20250515), which prints no JSON Schema, CDDL or ABNF of its own. Source .cache/w3c-vc-data-model-2-0.bin, sha256 a9196a3d0b6601356c4e127bad24f8c7f2c17f6ed22e41b35755a910104156f8; quotations («…») are copied by script from its rendering .cache/w3c-vc-data-model-2-0.txt, sha256 73d91cc0b6a7d582512eb06d45a5fcfa8c696ab094b3db44f7a1495e9d3da548, and carry their line. INSTANCE: the unsecured data model object as a JSON object (a credential or a presentation, with or without an embedded proof member). LEVELS: the root and every anchor not ending in -should state MUST and MUST NOT rules (non-conformance on failure); anchors ending in -should include the MUST level by reference and add SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and RECOMMENDED statements (a failure is a deviation to warn about, never non-conformance). A constraint marked INFERRED is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source; the cross-field-rules file carries what JSON Schema cannot express. USE: validate against an anchor, e.g. urn:library:w3c-vc-data-model-2-0:vcdm.derived#VerifiableCredential. The root is a document that is a VerifiableCredential, a VerifiablePresentation, an EnvelopedVerifiableCredential or an EnvelopedVerifiablePresentation, chosen by its type member.
title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0: credential, presentation, enveloped forms and their members (DERIVED)

url.$comment: MUST: «If present, id property's value MUST be a single URL, which MAY be dereferenceable.» (§4.4 L425) INFERRED: the source defines URL by the URL Standard (L282) and says issuer URLs identify the issuer "in a globally unambiguous way" (L1282); this schema reads that as an absolute URL, i.e. it has a scheme, and does not accept a relative reference. RECOMMENDED dereferenceability (L425) is not checkable here.

typeValue.$comment: MUST: «The value of the type property MUST be one or more terms and absolute URL strings.» (§4.5 L662) INFERRED: a term is any non-empty string without whitespace; whether a term is defined by the active context is a JSON-LD matter this schema cannot see. The order of values does not matter (L662).

dateTimeStamp.$comment: MUST: «If present, the value of the validFrom property MUST be a [XMLSCHEMA11-2] dateTimeStamp string value» (§4.9 L2030) The pattern is the regular expression of Example 32 (L3174-L3178, joined as the text instructs), anchored. The text says the expression in XMLSCHEMA11-2 is the normative definition and that the expression admits values that are not valid moments (e.g. 31 days in every month), so a match is necessary, not sufficient (cross-field rule X-02).

context.$comment: MUST: «The value of the @context property MUST be an ordered set where the first item is a URL with the value https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2. Subsequent items in the ordered set MUST be composed of any combination of URLs and objects, where each is processable as a JSON-LD Context.» (§4.3 L393) INFERRED: a bare string equal to the base URL is accepted as the one-item set (JSON-LD treats a single value as a set of one); an array must start with that URL. uniqueItems is INFERRED from the word set. That each later item is processable as a JSON-LD context is not checkable here (X-06).

context-should.$comment: SHOULD NOT: «A conforming document SHOULD NOT use the @vocab feature in production as it can lead to JSON term clashes, resulting in semantic ambiguities with other applications.» (§5.2 L2876) MUST: «If a conforming document does not use JSON-LD Contexts that define all terms used, it MUST include the https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/undefined-terms/v2 as the last value in the @context property.» (§5.2 L2876) The MUST is conditional on a fact about the terms (X-18) and is not checked here. INFERRED: the SHOULD NOT is read for inline context objects (an object item carrying @vocab); a @vocab inside a context reached by URL, such as the examples context, cannot be seen. Also read here: inline contexts are discouraged (L3262), not forbidden.

languageValueObject.$comment: MUST: «the object MUST contain a @value property whose value is a string» (§11.1 L3941) (§11 is marked non-normative, but §4.6 makes the form binding for name and description) MUST NOT: «The language value object MUST NOT include any other keys beyond @value, @language, and @direction.» (§11.1 L3941) MAY: «MAY contain a @direction property whose value is a base direction string defined by the @direction property in [JSON-LD11]» (§11.1 L3941) INFERRED: the base direction strings of JSON-LD 1.1 are ltr and rtl. The SHOULD for @language is in #languageValueObject-should.

languageValueObject-should.$comment: SHOULD: «and SHOULD contain a @language property whose value is a string containing a well-formed Language-Tag as defined by [BCP47]» (§11.1 L3941) INFERRED: well-formed is checked with the BCP47 section 2.1 syntax written as a regular expression (including the grandfathered tags of section 2.2.8); registry validity is not checked.

textValue.$comment: MUST: «If present, the value of the name property MUST be a string or a language value object as described in 11.1 Language and Base Direction.» (§4.6 L922) The same sentence is made for description (L924). TENSION T-03: §11.1 (L3961) says several language value objects MAY be given as an array value for the property, and §6 (L3240) says every property other than id, issuer, validFrom and validUntil may be an array; this MUST profile follows the strict §4.6 sentence and rejects an array. See README.

textValue-should.$comment: SHOULD: «The language and base direction of each natural language string property value SHOULD be provided, either via the language value structure for each property value, or via a default language and base direction for all values in the entire credential.» (§11.2 L4012) INFERRED: a bare string is accepted, because the document-default route (a default @language and @direction set in the context, X-14) is invisible to JSON Schema; a language value object must carry a well-formed @language.

textValueMulti.$comment: MAY: «Multiple language value objects MAY be provided as an array value for the property:» (§11.1 L3961) and MUST: «All other properties, if present, are represented as either a single value or an array of values.» (§6 L3240) READING B of tension T-03: name and description may be a string, a language value object, or a non-empty array of either. Example 6 (the source's own example) uses this form for name and description. Used only by #VerifiableCredential-arity.

issuerObject.$comment: MUST: an object containing an id property whose value is a URL (L1282). INFERRED: an issuer object is not required to carry type; the source names only id.

issuer.$comment: MUST: «The value of the issuer property MUST be either a URL or an object containing an id property whose value is a URL; in either case, the issuer selects this URL to identify itself in a globally unambiguous way.» (§4.7 L1282) The one-value arity of issuer is L3240.

subjectObject.$comment: MUST: «each object MUST be the subject of one or more claims, which MUST be serialized inside the credentialSubject property.» (§4.8 L1774) INFERRED: a subject object with no member other than id carries no claim, so it is rejected; whether type counts as a claim is not stated, it is accepted as one. Each object MAY contain an id (L1774) which follows §4.4.

credentialSubject.$comment: MUST: «The value of the credentialSubject property is a set of objects» (§4.8 L1774) A single object is accepted as a set of one (JSON-LD), an array needs at least one object.

statusObject.$comment: MUST: «The type property is REQUIRED.» (§4.10 L2276) MAY: «The id property is OPTIONAL.» (§4.10 L2274) Further members are defined by the status type (L2277), so they are open.

credentialStatus.$comment: MUST: «If present, the value associated with the credentialStatus property is a single object or a set of one or more objects.» (§4.10 L2272) NOTE: §4.2 lists the property as status (L375); every other place says credentialStatus (finding in contexts.yaml and README).

schemaObject.$comment: MUST: «Each credentialSchema MUST specify its type (for example, JsonSchema) and an id property that MUST be a URL identifying the schema file.» (§4.11 L2351)

credentialSchema.$comment: MUST: «The value of the credentialSchema property MUST be one or more data schemas» (§4.11 L2351)

refreshObject.$comment: MUST: «Each refreshService value MUST specify its type.» (§5.4 L2926)

refreshService.$comment: MUST: «The value of the refreshService property MUST be one or more refresh services» (§5.4 L2926)

termsObject.$comment: MUST: «Each termsOfUse value MUST specify its type, for example, TrustFrameworkPolicy, and MAY specify its instance id.» (§5.5 L2961)

termsOfUse.$comment: MUST: «The value of the termsOfUse property MUST specify one or more terms of use policies» (§5.5 L2961)

evidenceObject.$comment: MUST: «The type property is REQUIRED.» (§5.6 L3022) MAY: «The id property is OPTIONAL.» (§5.6 L3020)

evidence.$comment: MUST: «If present, the value of the evidence property MUST be either a single object or a set of one or more objects.» (§5.6 L3018)

reservedObject.$comment: MUST: «implementations MUST specify a type property in the value associated with the reserved property.» (§5.10 L3190) MUST: «The associated vocabulary URL MUST be https://www.w3.org/2018/credentials#confidenceMethod.» (§5.10 L3192) (for confidenceMethod; renderMethod L3193 likewise)

reservedProperty.$comment: Used for confidenceMethod and renderMethod, the two reserved extension points of §5.10 (L3191-L3193). INFERRED: the one-or-more arity follows L3240 (all other properties are single or array).

sriHashExpression.$comment: MUST: «One or more cryptographic digests, as defined by the hash-expression ABNF grammar defined in the Subresource Integrity specification, Section 3.5: The integrity attribute.» (§5.3 L2887) INFERRED from that ABNF (not reproduced in the source): hash-algo is sha256, sha384 or sha512; the base64 value has the exact length of that digest (43+pad, 64, 86+pad characters), so a value with an extra character is rejected; options after '?' are VCHAR. This length check is arithmetic, not a statement of the source.

sriString.$comment: MUST: «See the ABNF grammar, defining the integrity attribute in the [SRI] specification, for the restrictions on the string format.» (§B.3.1 L4146) INFERRED: one or more hash expressions separated by whitespace, or an array of them.

sriString-should.$comment: SHOULD: «At the time of this writing sha384 SHOULD be considered the minimum strength hash algorithm for use by implementers.» (§5.3 L2896) INFERRED: read as: every digest in digestSRI uses sha384 or sha512.

digestMultibase.$comment: MUST: «One or more cryptographic digests, as defined by the digestMultibase property in the Verifiable Credential Data Integrity 1.0 specification, Section 2.6: Resource Integrity.» (§5.3 L2888) INFERRED: only the container is checked (a multibase string of at least two characters, or a non-empty array of them); the multibase and multihash layers belong to the Data Integrity lane.

relatedResourceObject.$comment: MUST: «The identifier for the resource is REQUIRED and conforms to the format defined in Section 4.4 Identifiers.» (§5.3 L2885) MUST: «Each object associated with relatedResource MUST contain at least a digestSRI or a digestMultibase value.» (§5.3 L2889) MAY: «An OPTIONAL valid media type as listed in the IANA Media Types registry.» (§5.3 L2886) INFERRED: mediaType is checked as type/subtype syntax only. The uniqueness of id across the list is cross-field rule X-03.

relatedResourceObject-should.$comment: SHOULD level of the object: digestSRI uses sha384 or sha512 when present.

relatedResource.$comment: MUST: «The value of the relatedResource property MUST be one or more objects of the following form:» (§5.3 L2883)

proof.$comment: INFERRED, deliberately thin: proof is defined by Verifiable Credential Data Integrity 1.0, not by this source (L3232: The proof property as defined in [VC-DATA-INTEGRITY] MAY be used by the embedded securing mechanism.). Only the container shape is checked here: an object, or a non-empty array of objects, each with a type. The DI lane carries the proof schema.

VerifiableCredential.$comment: MUST: «Verifiable credentials and verifiable presentations MUST include a @context property.» (§4.3 L391) MUST: «Verifiable credentials and verifiable presentations MUST contain a type property with an associated value.» (§4.5 L660) MUST: «A verifiable credential MUST have an issuer property.» (§4.7 L1280) MUST: «A verifiable credential MUST contain a credentialSubject property.» (§4.8 L1772) The type must include VerifiableCredential (L892, the §4.5 table). Other members are open (extensibility, §5.2). The secured-ness of a conforming document (L228) is not a property of this object: see VerifiableCredential-embedded-proof and X-04. Properties named by §4.2 but not defined as JSON members here: none.

VerifiableCredential-arity.$comment: READING B of tension T-03 (see textValueMulti): identical to #VerifiableCredential except that name and description take #textValueMulti, following §6 (L3240) and §11.1 (L3961) and Example 6 over the strict sentence of §4.6. MUST: «Verifiable credentials and verifiable presentations MUST include a @context property.» (§4.3 L391) MUST: «Verifiable credentials and verifiable presentations MUST contain a type property with an associated value.» (§4.5 L660) MUST: «A verifiable credential MUST have an issuer property.» (§4.7 L1280) MUST: «A verifiable credential MUST contain a credentialSubject property.» (§4.8 L1772) The type must include VerifiableCredential (L892, the §4.5 table). Other members are open (extensibility, §5.2). The secured-ness of a conforming document (L228) is not a property of this object: see VerifiableCredential-embedded-proof and X-04. Properties named by §4.2 but not defined as JSON members here: none.

VerifiableCredential-should.$comment: SHOULD: «All credentials, presentations, and encapsulated objects SHOULD specify, or be associated with, additional, more narrow types (like ExampleDegreeCredential, for example) so software systems can more easily detect and process this additional information.» (§4.5 L908) INFERRED: read for the credential itself as at least one type value besides VerifiableCredential. Natural-language values SHOULD carry language (L4012): name and description use textValue-should. relatedResource uses the sha384 minimum (L2896). validFrom and validUntil are already MUST-level dateTimeStamp (L2030); SHOULD dateTimeStamp for all time values (L3169) concerns members this schema does not name.

VerifiableCredential-embedded-proof.$comment: MUST: «A conforming document MUST be secured by at least one securing mechanism as described in Section 4.12 Securing Mechanisms.» (§1.3 L228) A credential secured by an embedded proof (L2392) carries a proof member; an enveloping proof (JOSE, COSE, SD-JWT) leaves this object bare, so this anchor is for the embedded class only.

vcOrEnvelopedVC.$comment: MUST: «The value MUST be one or more verifiable credential and/or enveloped verifiable credential objects (the values MUST NOT be non-object values such as numbers, strings, or URLs).» (§4.13 L2475)

holder.$comment: MUST: «If present, the value MUST be either a URL or an object containing an id property.» (§4.13 L2477) INFERRED: the object form is checked as issuerObject is (an id that is a URL). L3240 would also allow an array of holders; the property definition (single value) is followed. TENSION T-03b.

VerifiablePresentation.$comment: MUST: «Verifiable credentials and verifiable presentations MUST include a @context property.» (§4.3 L391) MUST: «The type property MUST be present. It is used to express the type of verifiable presentation. One value of this property MUST be VerifiablePresentation, but additional types MAY be included.» (§4.13 L2473) MAY: «The verifiableCredential property MAY be present.» (§4.13 L2475) MAY: «The verifiable presentation MAY include a holder property.» (§4.13 L2477) The id is optional (L2471). Presentation termsOfUse is allowed (L2955, the holder places terms in the presentation). Other members open.

VerifiablePresentation-should.$comment: SHOULD: «All credentials, presentations, and encapsulated objects SHOULD specify, or be associated with, additional, more narrow types (like ExampleDegreeCredential, for example) so software systems can more easily detect and process this additional information.» (§4.5 L908) INFERRED: at least one type value besides VerifiablePresentation. That a presentation SHOULD be extremely short-lived and bound to a challenge (L2467) is not a property of the object.

EnvelopedVerifiableCredential.$comment: MUST: «The @context property of the object MUST be present and include a context, such as the base context for this specification, that defines at least the id, type, and EnvelopedVerifiableCredential terms as defined by the base context provided by this specification.» (§4.13 L2497) MUST: «The id value of the object MUST be a data: URL [RFC2397]» (§4.13 L2497) MUST: «The type value of the object MUST be EnvelopedVerifiableCredential.» (§4.13 L2497) INFERRED: the type value is read as the string EnvelopedVerifiableCredential itself (the examples all do), not an array; that the context defines the three terms (X-15) and that the data: URL holds a secured document (X-16) are not checked. The data: URL check is the RFC 2397 shape data:[mediatype][;base64],data.

EnvelopedVerifiablePresentation.$comment: MUST: «The @context property of the object MUST be present and include a context, such as the base context for this specification, that defines at least the id, type, and EnvelopedVerifiablePresentation terms as defined by the base context provided by this specification.» (§4.13 L2521) MUST: «The id value of the object MUST be a data: URL [RFC2397]» (§4.13 L2521) MUST: «The type value of the object MUST be EnvelopedVerifiablePresentation.» (§4.13 L2521) INFERRED: the type value is read as the string EnvelopedVerifiablePresentation itself (the examples all do), not an array; that the context defines the three terms (X-15) and that the data: URL holds a secured document (X-16) are not checked. The data: URL check is the RFC 2397 shape data:[mediatype][;base64],data.
